quote: So there was, like, three people at my house with different solar, ideas.
stewart_read: Customer discloses three competing solar visits (including a water softener bundle) but rep never asks which companies or what was shown.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be strategically avoiding a competitive rabbit hole to keep the call moving — but nothing later shows this was deliberate; he simply moves to a generic 'is it something you're still thinking about' question.
coaching_implication: Probe which companies and what was proposed — this is competitive intel and a curiosity-creation opening the rep left on the table.

quote: now what we do is we do a bill swap. So instead of adding another bill to your plate, we're taking away your electric bill
stewart_read: This is the clearest inversion move in the call — reframing 'can't add a bill' into 'we're swapping your existing bill,' matching the schema's flip pattern even without an actual bill number captured.
coaching_implication: Good execution of strategy without a number to anchor it — would land harder if rep had actually captured the electric bill amount first.

quote: No. It's just something I'm I'm gonna have to discuss with my my other half.
stewart_read: Rep says 'For sure' but does not immediately pivot to including the partner on the appointment — that only happens two exchanges later after the email deflection.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have been building toward the phone-call-with-partner offer he makes at 03:47, so this could be a deliberate sequencing choice rather than a miss.
coaching_implication: Should reflexively say 'let's get your partner on the call too' at the moment the spouse is mentioned, not wait for the customer to try to exit first.

quote: Is there any way you can email me and just so I can discuss it? I'm driving right now.
stewart_read: This is the email-before-meeting hard rule; rep does hold the line correctly by declining pure email and offering a phone-call structure instead.
coaching_implication: Correct handling — flag as a positive example of holding the hard rule while still offering an alternative path.

quote: Can we do so since I'm already off Monday and Tuesday this week, is there anything we could do probably possibly Tuesday or Wednesday of next week?
stewart_read: Customer proactively offers his own schedule availability, showing renewed engagement after the earlier deflection attempt.
coaching_implication: Rep should reinforce this momentum by immediately locking a specific time and reconfirming the partner's presence in the same breath.

quote: I think we'll have our our specialist come by just because, you know, phone call is kind of our last resort.
stewart_read: After the customer explicitly said phone call would 'always be better,' rep unilaterally switches the appointment to in-person without re-confirming, and the call ends without the one-hour block, no-driving reminder, or 'is that fair' handshake.
coaching_implication: Button-up is incomplete — no explicit re-confirmation of channel with customer buy-in, no time-block statement, no verbal handshake before ending the call.
